Paper 2.13: 'dox-treated cells were kept in RPMI SILAC medium supplemented with heavy-labeled amino acids (Arg10, Lys8, Leu6) and dox'. Cross-check: median log2 H/M of HLA peptides = 0.10 / 0.09 (scr 24h/48h) vs 1.09 / 1.44 (p14 24h/48h), matching the paper's 'global immunopeptidome enhances upon p14 kd'; MDA peptides go down only in p14 (PMEL median log2 H/M -0.97/-0.51, DCT -2.09/-2.52) vs scr (PMEL 0.26/-0.14, DCT 0.44/0.70), matching Fig. 4C. Heavy = dox (knockdown-induced) is consistent.

Paper 2.13: 'whereas untreated cells were kept in medium with medium-heavy-labeled amino acids (Arg6, Lys4, Leu3)'. MaxQuant multiplicity 3 with medium = Arg6/Lys4/Leu3. SILAC light channel (pre-existing, unlabelled material from both mixed cultures in this pulsed design) is not a sample and is not annotated; see limitations.

Rule 1: spec README.adoc:27 Version v1.1.0.
Template versions per sdrf-tools contract and upstream templates.yaml. clinical-metadata declared solely to license characteristics[genotype] and characteristics[dose].
Rule 10.
Filled by sdrf-tools build from ms-proteomics.
Each sample was injected once per method; there are no repeated measurements of the same precursor population.
Meth10J runs (36992/36997/37002/37007): z=2 only, MS1 376-801 (e.g. 36992 has 2052 z=2 vs 3 z=3 evidences). MaxQuant Fraction 101-104 within each sample's Experiment.

Meth13K runs (36993/36998/37003/37008) 'charge1und3': z=1 and z=3 (e.g. 36993 has 792 z=1, 530 z=3, 15 z=2), MS1 251-1601. MaxQuant Fraction 201-204 in the same Experiment, so the authors combined the charge-state split as fractions. Same-lab PXD054097 encodes this method pair as fraction 1/2.
Meth13K Method Summary (36993, 37008): a z=3 MS2 scan event with 'ActivationType = ETD' in addition to stepped HCD. MS:1000598 verified live. Repeated column as in PXD054097.
Meth10J runs have a single HCD MS2 event and no ETD.

Paper 2.1: knockdown induced with 2 ug/mL doxycycline for six days (renewed at day four). Paper 2.13: the dox-treated (heavy) cultures were kept in heavy medium with dox during the pulse. CHEBI:50845 'doxycycline'. Licensed by clinical-metadata. Medium rows: not applicable.

limitations: SILAC light channel not annotated: in this pulsed SILAC design the light (Arg0/Lys0/Leu0) signal is pre-existing material from BOTH 1:1-mixed cultures, not a sample; MaxQuant quantified with multiplicity 3 but only H/M ratios were used (paper 2.13). Following the same lab's curated precedents PXD054097 and PXD051190 (medium + heavy rows only). 16 rows = 8 RAW x 2 channels.

The two runs per sample are a charge-state split of one sample: Meth10J is z=2 (MS1 376-801); Meth13K is z=1 and z=3 (MS1 251-1601) and adds an ETD MS2 event. They are encoded as fraction 1/2 with technical replicate 1, following MaxQuant's Fraction 1xx/2xx in one Experiment and the same-lab PXD054097. There is no physical fractionation, so comment[fractionation method] is omitted (no PRIDE:0000550 child describes a charge-state acquisition split).

Two values differ between the fractions of one source: comment[ms1 scan range] and a second comment[dissociation method] column (the contract's dissociation method column is not 'multiple'). sdrf-tools build cannot vary a column between the fractions of one samples.tsv row, so these are set by the deterministic, asserting postbuild.py step recorded in validation.txt round 2.

Dox exposure: the dox-treated cultures were pre-induced with 2 ug/mL dox for 6 days (renewed at day 4; paper 2.1) before the 24/48 h pulse, during which dox was continued (2.13). characteristics[sampling time] gives only the pulse time. Total dox exposure is about 7-8 days and is not encoded as exposure duration, because the paper does not state it as a single number.

Supplementary Table S1 (s003.xlsx) could not be re-fetched by this producer: Europe PMC supplementaryFiles returned errorBean 'Connection refused' twice in round 2. The HLA phenotype and the University Hospital Essen source rely on the reviewer's quotation. The HLA alleles are independently corroborated by Fig. 4A and the Peptide-PRISM allele column.

No mqpar.xml / parameters.txt deposited: precursor 4.5 ppm and fragment 20 ppm are MaxQuant 2.0 defaults inferred from the paper's 'MaxQuant default parameters'; PEAKS Xpro tolerances (identification search) are not reported.

Two searches were used: PEAKS Xpro de novo + Peptide-PRISM (identification, 10% FDR) and MaxQuant 2.0 (H/M quantification). Both declare the same variable mods (Carbamidomethyl C, Oxidation M, Gln->pyro-Glu, 6 SILAC labels); the encoded set is read from MQ_evidence.txt.

Antibody used for the HLA-I immunoprecipitation is not stated in this paper (W6/32 appears only as a blocking antibody in cocultures); Methods defer to Bernhardt et al. Anal Chem 2022 (doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.2c02198), closed access (Unpaywall oa_status closed). characteristics[antibody enrichment] = not available.
MHC typing method not stated; HLA-C alleles not reported (typing lists A and B only) -> mhc typing method = not available.

Reduction/alkylation not described for the immunopeptidome prep (the DTT/IAA statement in 2.13 belongs to the proteome analysis, whose runs are not deposited); Carbamidomethyl is a variable search mod only -> reduction/alkylation reagent = not available.

Proteome (gel-slice, trypsin) pSILAC runs described in paper 2.13 are not part of this deposit (only 8 HLA-peptide RAW files, all mapped in sample_overview.xlsx), so no trypsin/label-free part exists.

Channel map assumed identical for all four samples (no label swap described); confirmed by data for heavy=dox in p14 samples (H/M up globally, MDA peptides down). In scr samples H/M ~ 1, so a swap there would not be detectable from ratios; rests on the paper's single stated design and sample_overview.
